_doc: THE DERIVED RESEARCH LAYER, AND THE COMMAND THAT REBUILDS EACH PART OF IT. Read by tools/rederive.mjs, which .github/steward/pr-lap.sh calls when a merge conflicts. WHY THIS EXISTS (owner, 2026-09-10): with the lap finally able to merge at all (PR #1058), every remaining open PR was left alone for a REAL CONFLICT, and every conflicting file was a tool output two runs had each re-derived — directory crosswalks, the land-sale spend, identity_master. pr-lap.sh already draws exactly the right line for this: 'A conflict here is never resolved by hand: the merge takes either side to clear the marker and the tool then rewrites the file from source.' It just drew it around five bookkeeping files. This file widens it, EXPLICITLY, so the widening is auditable rather than a glob nobody can audit.
_the_rule: A path under `resolves` may have its conflict cleared by taking either side, because a step below rewrites it from its inputs. A path NOT listed here is refused exactly as before — that is the whole safety property, and it is why this file enumerates rather than pattern-matches. `resolves: []` means the step runs to keep the tree consistent but resolves no conflict: its outputs are still content a run may have meant to change.
_the_backstop: Nothing here is trusted on its say-so. After the sequence runs, tools/check.sh must pass, and it is check.sh that asserts each of these files re-derives from its inputs. A wrong entry here makes the gate RED, and pr-lap.sh does not push a red tree. The failure mode is a PR that stays open — the one it was already in — never a bad merge onto dev.
_only_gated_tools: A step may only appear here if tools/check.sh runs its tool with --check. That invariant is enforced by rederive.mjs --check, and it is not decoration — it is the whole reason the backstop above is real. Learned by nearly shipping the opposite: crosswalk_norris_1844_advertiser.py was in this file on first draft, and running it rebuilt norris_1844_advertiser_crosswalk_1835.json from 443 lines to 195, taking data/residents/directories.json down with it. check.sh did not invoke that tool AT ALL, so nothing in the gate would have gone red and the lap would have pushed the loss. An ungated derivation is one whose committed file nobody has ever asserted re-derives, and this file may not resolve a conflict by re-running one. READ THAT IN THE PAST TENSE: T-0867 gated the advertising crosswalk for the same reason, and it is listed below now. The example stands as the reason for the rule, not as a live claim about that tool — check what check.sh runs today, never what this sentence remembers.
_must_actually_write: A step's command must WRITE the files it claims. Obvious, and it is the one thing --check cannot see by reading, so `rederive.mjs --prove` runs every command and asserts each `resolves` file's mtime advanced. It exists because read_newberry_index.py was listed here for `data/research/newberry_index/leads.json` and, invoked bare, PRINTS ITS USAGE AND EXITS 0 — it writes nothing, and rebuilding leads.json needs --parse over OCR shards that live outside the repo. The bad entry survived a --check (the tool is gated), an idempotency test (nothing changed, because nothing ran) and a full-sequence run. It failed only when a real merge needed it, as `leads.json does not re-derive from its inputs`. The idempotency test that missed it used `timeout 400` with output suppressed, so a killed tool and a no-op tool looked identical. Run --prove when this file changes; a tool that needs inputs from outside the repo does not belong here at all.
_must_reproduce: AND A GATED TOOL THAT PASSES --check MAY STILL NOT BELONG HERE, which is the rule `_only_gated_tools` does not cover and the one that nearly admitted two more files on 2026-09-14. `--check` asks whether the committed OUTCOMES still follow from the inputs; a manifest entry resolves a conflict by re-running the BUILD and keeping whatever it writes. Those are different questions and they can disagree. Measured on a clean `dev` that afternoon: `crosswalk_census_1840_heads.py --check` reported `OK: 965 named 1840 head(s) — 13 matched, 18 candidate, 934 refused` and exited 0, while `--build` on the SAME TREE rewrote 137 lines of census_1840/crosswalk.json and resident_crosswalk.json — rule prose and evidence lists that had drifted, picking up the 1844 directory and a fourth Sherman. Nothing is stale by the gate's measure and the file still does not rebuild to itself. Listing it would have made the lap push those 137 lines into EVERY pull request it lapped, as a silent content change no ticket asked for. So before adding a step: run its command on a clean base and require that git reports NOTHING moved. A green --check is necessary and it is not sufficient.
_a_card_is_its_own_input: A FILE THAT IS ITS OWN INPUT IS NOT DERIVED, HOWEVER CLEANLY IT REPRODUCES — and that is the case `_must_reproduce` does not decide, measured for T-1282 on 2026-10-04. The question was whether the household cards under data/residents/households/ could be listed against `derive_resident_roles.py --write`, so that a pull request conflicting on an hh_*.json stops being refused whole. On a clean `dev` (d092128d) `--check` reported `738 role(s) stand on the cards, and every one of them re-derives`, and `--write` on the same tree reported `wrote 0 card(s)` with git showing nothing moved: the step passes `_must_reproduce` outright. It is still not listed, and the reason is `_the_rule`'s own premise. A listed path may be cleared by taking either side BECAUSE a step below rewrites it from its inputs; the roles tool reads each card's evidence and writes `roles[]` and `occupation` back into the SAME card, so the card is the input and the step owns two keys of it. The lap clears a listed conflict with `git checkout --ours`, which keeps the branch's whole card and drops whatever the base changed in it — an evidence row, a ruling's note, a presence argument — and the rebuild then re-derives the roles from the card that survived. `--check` re-derives against that same card, so it reads green: the backstop cannot see the loss, which is the one failure `_the_backstop` was never built to catch. Other blocks on a card are written by other tools (107 tools touch the card folder; staff_businesses_1835.py's persons[].workplaces and spend_old_settlers.py's block are among the 43 gated writers audit_manifest_coverage.mjs counts as not yet placed), so even a card all of whose keys had a writer would be a merge of many owners, not one step's output. So a household-card conflict stays refused, on purpose, and rederive.mjs --self-test holds that no path under data/residents/households/ is ever listed. What would change the answer is the card ceasing to be its own input — derived blocks moved into files a step owns outright — and that is a restructuring, not a manifest line.
_never: A file declaring `hand_authored: true` is refused even if listed. data/research/land_sales/resident_rulings.json is the one such file today: a judgement is not a derivation, and re-running a tool over it would erase the argument. rederive.mjs --check fails if any listed path declares it.
_a_reader_sits_below_what_it_reads: A STEP THAT READS A FILE ANOTHER STEP REBUILDS SAYS SO, AND --check HOLDS IT BELOW THAT STEP (T-2080). The sequence is a measured order, not a graph, so an edge nobody wrote down is an edge the next insertion can break without a sound: on a clean tree every committed file already agrees with its inputs and a reader placed above its writer passes, and the lag shows only on a MERGED tree, as a refusal that reads like a data fault (`location_spend.py` refusing a business whose seat had moved, T-1720) or, worse, as a stale file written without complaint (`report_convergence_coverage.py`). `reads` on a step lists files it reads that the manifest also resolves; check() requires each to be rebuilt by a step ABOVE it, and requires the reader's own source to name the file, so a declaration cannot be cargo. A lag the order cannot remove — a cycle — is not declared here; it is `second_pass` with `reads_rebuilt`, which is the same edge stated from the other side. Not every edge is declared yet: a scan of each tool's source for the basenames of files resolved below it names about 48 candidates, most of them reads of sources/index.json for citation checks, and each has to be read before it is written down.
_the_second_pass: A STEP THAT READS A FILE A LATER STEP REBUILDS IS ONE MODEL BEHIND WHEN THE SEQUENCE ENDS, AND `--run` TWICE DOES NOT FIX IT (T-1363). The sequence below is a measured order, not a graph — its own `_doc` says so — and this is the edge it cannot express. `reconstruct_residents_1835.py --stage attribute_fill_arrival` DRAWS from data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json, and model_town_1835.py rebuilds that model from the population the stage itself writes into. So any run that moves the population leaves the arrival draws standing on the model as it was BEFORE the move, and `reconstruct_residents_1835.py --check` goes red on roughly 1,400 cards with 'the committed value does not re-derive from the programme'. Measured on #1495 (T-1172, 2026-09-19) three times over, and reproduced deterministically for T-1363 on 2026-09-21 by moving one weight in arrival_year_of_the_known_layer: one full pass left 1,434 red assertions, and the three commands below cleared every one of them and returned the tree byte-identical to dev. RE-ORDERING CANNOT FIX IT: the model is derived FROM the layer the arrival stage writes into, so moving the stage below the model trades the lag for the opposite lag. A declared second pass can, because it is the cycle walked once more from a settled model, and tools/check.sh is the proof that it settles — model, profile, tiers and residents all --check green afterwards, which is what convergence means here. Entries run AFTER every step, in the order written, and each must name a step above: the second pass re-runs the sequence's own commands and admits no tool the sequence has not already gated and proven. The first entry carries `reads_rebuilt` — the file whose rebuild is the lag — and --check asserts a later step really does resolve it, so an entry cannot claim a lag that is not there. The entries after it carry no `reads_rebuilt` because their reason is different and one step removed: they are the repairs the lagging reader's rewrite makes necessary, so they must follow it. T-1602 ADDED A SECOND LAGGING READER AND PUT IT FIRST: the model reads the scene's people.json and the town census, both rebuilt below it, so it is rebuilt from them before the arrival stage draws from it. Any entry may carry `reads_rebuilt`; --check holds each one to a step below it that really rebuilds the file.

second_pass.why: THE MODEL IS ITSELF A LAGGING READER, and it has to lead (T-1602). model_town_1835.py reads data/sidecars/1835/people.json and data/town_census.json, which compile_scene.py and town_census.py rebuild 23 and 49 steps BELOW it, and town_census.py reads the model back, so no linear order settles the pair. On a branch that moves the population the sequence builds the model from the PRE-merge scene; the arrival stage then re-draws from that stale model and the run ends red on the model and on every card it re-drew. Measured 2026-10-04 on dev with people.json, town_census.json and the model taken from before #344 (the shape of a lap that kept a branch's side): one --run left `model_town_1835.py --check` red and 427 files off dev; this entry first, then the three below, returned the cards, model, profile and tiers byte-identical to dev. It goes FIRST because the arrival stage draws from what it writes.

THE LAGGING READER, and the whole reason this pass exists. The stage draws arrival_year and reason_for_coming from the town model's arrival_year_of_the_known_layer and birthplace_of_the_old_settlers_who_came_by_1835 tables; model_town_1835.py rebuilds that model further down the sequence, from a profile of the very cards this stage writes. Drawn once more from the settled model, the draws reproduce. Since T-1602 it runs AFTER the model is rebuilt from the settled scene, which is what lets it draw from a model that matches the population rather than the one the sequence started from.
Downstream of the re-draw above: the tier table is derived per-attribute from the resident layer, so it moves whenever a card does, and the re-draw moves ~1,400 of them.

Also downstream of the re-draw, and LAST by measurement rather than by taste: this is the order that converged by hand on #1495 and again under T-1363's reproduction. It profiles the population the re-draw just moved; the model it feeds is then asserted unmoved by model_town_1835.py --check in the gate, which is the statement that the cycle has settled rather than merely turned.

THE SEATING CHAIN'S BACKWARD EDGE (T-2081). The platted deal reads the address book, which seat_known_1835.py rebuilds below it from the seats this deal wrote, so no linear order settles the pair (the one that puts the address book first refuses outright — see the chain's step). What travels back is small: each seat copies its household's display name out of the address book. Measured 2026-10-04 with the chain's seven outputs taken from before #396 and everything else at dev: one walk of the chain left exactly two seats behind — hh_ambrose_joshua and hh_bradford_harriet still named 'a name from the post office's letter lists', the name T-1689 (#398) had already changed on their cards — and the seat checks red; this entry and the next cleared both, and the tree came back byte-identical to dev with seat_known, both deals, the order book, compile_liberties, house_the_present and seat_trade_roofs all --check green. compile_liberties.py and seat_trade_roofs_1835.py also read the seats and were NOT moved by that difference. A later perturbation (T-2082) did move seat_trade_roofs_1835.py, and it joined this pass below; compile_liberties.py stayed still under that one too, and after_the_pass.between holds it to that answer.
The off-plat deal's scope is the platted deal's `owed` list, so it follows the entry above whenever that one re-runs (T-2081).

THE ONE STEP BETWEEN THE PASS AND THE TAIL THAT MOVES WITH IT (T-2082). seat_trade_roofs_1835.py writes each off-plat adoption's household name into the note of a roof it declines ("The off-plat deal (T-1614) adopted it for The Miller and Hall tannery household, but ..."), so when the deal above re-runs and a name travels back from the address book, this step is left one name behind and nothing re-runs it: the tail starts below it. Measured 2026-10-04 by renaming two households in each seat file by hand: of the 47 steps that sat between the pass and the tail, this was the only one whose --check went red (`1835_trade_roof_seats.json is stale`), and --build moved exactly that note. T-2081's reproduction did not move it because no name it moved was an off-plat adoption's. It follows the off-plat deal because that is what it reads.

_after_the_pass: AND THEN THE SCENE, UNTIL IT STOPS MOVING (T-1602). The second pass rewrites resident cards, so everything from compile_scene.py down is standing on cards that have since moved; that is why pr-lap.sh re-ran `--tail tools/compile_scene.py` after every `--run`, and why a person running `--run` alone was left one hand step short of a green gate. One tail is not always enough either, because the scene and its generators are a CYCLE of their own: compile_scene.py reads the structure records generate_block_infill.py and its siblings write (their fabric rule reads each household's arrival), and those generators read the sidecars compile_scene.py writes. Measured 2026-10-04 on the same reproduction as the model entry above: after the pass, one tail left 8 sidecars and town_yard_outbuildings.json a lap behind their structures, and a second tail returned the tree byte-identical to dev. So `--run` (and every `--tail` and `--resolve`) repeats the tail from `tail_from` until a lap changes nothing in the tree, at most `max_laps` times. A settled tree costs one lap: the lap that proves nothing moved. THE STEPS BETWEEN THE PASS AND THE TAIL ARE A MEASURED ANSWER, AND IT IS GATED (T-2082, T-1671's step 3). The pass re-runs its own steps, and the tail re-runs everything from `tail_from` down, but the steps that sit below the pass's first step and above `tail_from` are run once, before the pass, and never again. Each one is safe there only if what the pass moves does not move it. Reading the source cannot settle that: followed through its imports, nearly every one of them reads the resident cards. So it was measured, by perturbing what the pass writes and asking --check of each step. `between` records the date, the perturbations and the steps found still. rederive.mjs --check refuses a step in that window that the answer does not list, and a listed step that has left it. So the next step inserted there fails until someone measures it the same way. A step that DOES move does not get listed: it joins the pass or goes below the tail. The first measurement found one, seat_trade_roofs_1835.py, and it joined the pass.

after_the_pass.why: compile_scene.py is the first step below the second pass that reads the resident cards it rewrites, and the step pr-lap.sh has always re-run late (T-1661).

between.how: Two perturbations of what the pass writes, each on a clean dev tree, each followed by every step below with its own check.sh line (python3 <tool> --check), 2 minutes 30 for the lot. (1) THE ARRIVAL DRAWS, the pass's reason for existing: 150 of arrival_year_of_the_known_layer's 1835 people moved to 1833 in data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json, then the pass's arrival stage, migrate_attribute_tiers.py and profile_population_1835.py rebuilt from it (383 files moved: the cards' arrival draws, the tier table, the profile). Every step below stayed green. Control: generate_block_infill.py, below the tail, went red on the same tree, so the checks do see the move. (2) THE SEATS, what the seating chain's backward edge carries (T-2081: display names out of the address book): two households renamed in data/reconstruction/1835_platted_seats.json and two in 1835_off_plat_seats.json. Every step below stayed green. seat_trade_roofs_1835.py went red, and it joined the pass instead of this list. Before that, every step here was green on clean dev. To measure a step you add here, run both perturbations, --check it, and restore the tree with git checkout. It is evidence over two perturbations, not a proof over every input, and it is now evidence that a new step cannot skip. settle_family_cycle.py (T-2234, measured 2026-10-09): under both perturbations its --check, the six --checks of the stages it drives, and a --build that settled in one lap moving nothing, all on the perturbed tree.

declared_readers.python3 tools/build_order_book_1835.py -: Reads both seat files' slot and seat counts, which the two deals in the pass rewrite. What the pass carries back through them is display names (T-2081): two names changed in each seat file left its --check green, and so did T-2081's chain reproduction.
declared_readers.python3 tools/seat_known_1835.py --build: Reads the town model (rewritten by the pass's first entry) and both seat files (rewritten by the deals). The model: with 150 of the arrival table's 1835 people moved to 1833 and the arrival stage, tiers and profile rebuilt from it, its --check stayed green, and #382's reproduction (the model rebuilt from a pre-#344 scene) ended with the tree byte-identical to dev. The seats: two names changed in each seat file left it green.
declared_readers.python3 tools/compile_liberties.py: Reads both seat files, which the deals in the pass rewrite. T-2081's chain reproduction did not move it, and two names changed in each seat file left its --check green.

_a_writer_belongs_here: IF YOU ADD A GATED WRITER, ADD IT HERE, AND THAT IS ENFORCED RATHER THAN ASKED. A tool check.sh runs with --check, and which can also --build or --write, produces DERIVED content by definition: if this file has never heard of it, rederive.mjs never runs it, pr-lap.sh leaves every open PR stale against it, and the gate goes red with no automated remedy and no clue in the message. Owner, 2026-09-18, after four separate hand-fixes in one night on exactly that — derive_resident_roles.py went red on FOUR merges, location_spend.py on the splitter change, profile_population_1835.py and model_town_1835.py the same night: "add a note to things to say if you add a writer it should be in that manifest, right?" A note is what this preamble already was, and it did not hold. tools/audit_manifest_coverage.mjs is the gate: every gated writer is listed here, or it is in that file's NOT_DERIVABLE list with the measurement that says why it cannot be. It found four MORE on the day it was written. Before listing anything, measure what `_must_reproduce` asks: run the build on a clean tree and confirm it changes no committed byte. A tool that does not reproduce belongs in the exemption list, never here.

steps.why: A SOURCE READ OUT OF ITS COMMITTED ORIGINAL. Nothing in the layer above it exists until this has run, so it sits with the other readers at the head of the manifest. PLACED BY LAYER, NOT BY A DERIVED DEPENDENCY (T-1302 batch 2, 2026-09-18). A dependency graph was built for this — write-sets MEASURED by running all 142 tools on a clean tree, reads taken from their source — and it was rejected by its own validation: against the 54 steps already here, an order people reached by hitting real failures, the graph contradicted 127 of 349 edges (36%; 32% at the finest granularity tried). These tools overwhelmingly read and write the same shared directories, so the graph saturates and cannot tell a real dependency from co-location. Only 6 of the 89 could be placed with evidence. A clean-tree `--run` goes green in ANY order because every one of them reproduces, so greenness is not evidence here either. This position is reasoned from what the tool reads and writes; it is not measured, and the honest test is the first time a change upstream of one of these fails to propagate. WRITES, BUT DOES NOT CLAIM, ITS OUTPUTS. `resolves` is not documentation: it declares that the manifest OWNS a file, so the lap settles a conflict there by REBUILDING rather than merging. Listing what these 89 tools touch took the owned set from 72 files to 1,899 — including 1,261 household cards — and a conflict in any of them would then be rebuilt over whatever a branch had actually written. Being run by the manifest and owning your outputs are separate decisions; this is the first, and the second is not taken here. rederive.mjs's own self-test caught it, on the assertion that `hh_taylor_c.json` is a file nobody derives.
